report:
Reviewed the complete immutable_entries claim, three ordinary implementation associations, and all three ordinary annotated tests. No TODO/N/A entries are present. The requirements are that existing scalar and slice allocations stay immutable, allocation may append without changing existing values, safe access cannot mutate interned contents, and transient inference is resolved and copied into a fresh completed-output stash.

Storage implementation: sage-stash/src/lib.rs keeps Stash storage, entry metadata, and handle indices private. Its public indexing implements Index only, yielding shared references; there is no IndexMut or public mutable-buffer access. StashData requires Copy, which excludes directly stored interior-mutability cells. alloc and alloc_slice return matching existing entries on deduplication or call push_raw to append padded data and metadata. AlignedBuf growth copies the old prefix unchanged, and suffix writes do not overwrite live entries. append_one copies into temporary values then allocates a new slice. These operations preserve existing interned values while permitting allocation growth.

Finalization implementation: finalize_typed_body creates a new Stash, takes the source only by shared reference, copies the root recursively, allocates locals and TyBodyData in the new stash, and returns Stashed ownership of that output. copy_ty first resolves the representative with VersionedEGraph::find at ROOT, recursively copies type edges and aliases, and rejects residual InferVar values. The captured and newly associated egraph implementation follows parent links through get_parent without mutating source allocations. copy_expr resolves transient slots, recursively rebuilds expression, statement, pattern, call-target and collection edges, and preserves sharing through copy maps. Consequently resolution changes output content rather than mutating previously interned input entries.

Test adequacy: appending_and_deduplicating_preserves_existing_entries saves a scalar and slice, allocates 4096 further values, checks both original contents, and checks that equal subsequent allocations return their original handles. safe_api_rejects_mutating_interned_scalars_and_slices includes exact fixture text in visible assertions and executes both trybuild rejection cases. Captured fixture diagnostics specifically require rejection because Stash has no IndexMut, covering both scalar assignment and indexed slice assignment. finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop unifies an inference variable to an imported Bool, finalizes a nested tuple with repeated child expressions, asserts the original inference allocation and both original slices remain unchanged, drops all source ownership and inference state, and then asserts the output types resolve to Bool, literals/spans survive, and repeated children share an output handle. These assertions would detect destructive in-place resolution, a missing deep copy, failure to resolve nested inference, or mutation during growth. This is a source assessment of the entire claim, with representative nested finalization coverage rather than a claim that every IR variant was independently executed.

Commands actually executed: cargo test -p sage-stash --test storage_contracts passed all 9 tests, including both trybuild cases; cargo test -p sage-ir finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop passed its one selected test. Added only an implementation-association comment above VersionedEGraph::find with coordinator authorization, ran cargo fmt, and restarted the review so the report covers the new association and fresh inputs. No behavioral implementation changes were made. Additional consulted source dependencies are captured in the initial implementation files and fixture reads.
